answer: Authenticated garbling adds MACs to every wire label, and the tide of the scheme is that a tampered label is detected before the output is released. The whisper of the design is that the garbler cannot change the circuit after the evaluator commits to its inputs, which blocks selective-failure attacks. When a group uses this to test identity uniqueness, a jetty of malicious participants cannot learn which honest inputs matched, and the result is trusted because every label was authenticated.
